The Nordics are one of Europe’s fastest growing hubs for infrastructure. AI clouds are expanding with a projected 1 gigawatts of capacity to be deployed across the region by the end of 2027. Among these cloud providers are Bitdeer, CoreWeave, Crusoe, Hyperstack, Nscale, Verda and Volta.

The consortium will build services using NVIDIA Nemotron open models, which allow researchers to customize and deploy their models in a secure environment.

articles.title: À court de cartes graphiques, Apple réquisitionne les Mac de ses employés
articles.summary:
Les ingénieurs d’Apple viennent de documenter Minions, un système interne qui met au travail les GPU inutilisés des Mac de l’entreprise. Le principe tient en une phrase des auteurs : « un nuage GPU virtuel, dynamique et distribué, qui agrège les GPU Apple Silicon inactifs des machines macOS pour exécuter des charges d’inférence d’apprentissage automatique à grande échelle ». Avant son déploiement, certaines tâches attendaient plus de dix heures en file, faute de GPU disponibles dans le parc centralisé ; elles démarrent désormais, le plus souvent, en quelques minutes.
Quatre rouages et un chien de garde
Le dispositif repose sur quatre composants. Un serveur central, le Minion Server, reçoit les requêtes des équipes et les découpe en sous-tâches, dont l’état est consigné dans une base PostgreSQL. Sur chaque Mac enrôlé, un Minion Executor exécute sa part du calcul sur le GPU local, téléverse le résultat vers un stockage S3 et rend compte au serveur.
Un chien de garde, le Minion Watchdog, surveille l’ensemble : si une machine cesse de répondre, ses tâches sont réattribuées ailleurs. Des tableaux de bord offrent une visibilité en temps réel sur l’état du troupeau.
Les Mac mini et Mac Studio récents savent par ailleurs s’associer via RDMA sur Thunderbolt 5, en combinant mémoire et puissance de calcul pour charger un modèle trop volumineux pour une seule machine.

Local and Distributed Large LLM Inference with MLX and RDMA on Mac Studio
MLX on Mac with Apple silicon lets AI researchers and developers experiment locally with the latest models and methods in a private environment. The open-source array framework leverages the unified memory architecture of Apple silicon, enabling anyone to run new inference and fine-tuning methods on their own hardware and explore other AI techniques. In a previous post, we highlighted the advantages of the M5 architecture and its GPU Neural Accelerators.
In this post, we show how to run the latest frontier-class model — Muse Spark Open, with nearly a trillion parameters — right from your desk, using the latest version of MLX, released today. On a cluster of four Mac Studios, Muse Spark Open generates over 36 tokens per second (see Figure 1), well above average human reading speed.

articles.title: What the West can learn from AI optimists in the rest of the world
articles.summary:
On a recent Sunday afternoon, I was invited to debate AI’s impact on the cultural sector alongside Dutch politicians and creative-industry leaders. I was the lone optimist, arguing that if fear and risk become our primary lens for governing artificial intelligence, we will design systems around what we want to prevent rather than what we want to use them for. Then I said something that was harder for the room to hear: The Global South is home to some of AI’s most enthusiastic and inventive users, and their experiments could help us rethink our own institutions.
The U.S. is no different from Europe. A culture of fear encourages protectionism: We hunker down and romanticize legacy systems rather than ask what might replace them. Creative industries in the majority world have spent decades navigating piracy and weak enforcement, forcing them to think beyond rights-based policing about how creators actually receive value. Anghami, the biggest music app in the Middle East, for instance, pays musicians from their first stream, rather than only after a song reaches a minimum threshold. It has approached AI pragmatically, using it to curate, tag, and attribute creative work rather than simply blocking and banning.
In the West, fear of AI has helped turn pessimism into a cultural virtue. Would you publicly say you love AI? Your answer may say something about where you’re from. Say “yes” to a concerned audience in the U.S. or the Netherlands, and you risk being seen as naive, or compli…

articles.title: LF Decentralized Trust Demonstrates the First Open Source Verifiable Trust Community in Prague
articles.summary:
LF Decentralized Trust Demonstrates the First Open Source Verifiable Trust Community in Prague
Drummond Reed, DTGWG co-chair; Glenn Gore, Geoff Turk, Brendan Miller and Alberto Leon, OpenVTC maintainers; and Hart Montgomery, LFDT CTO | 15 October 2026
Two LF Decentralized Trust (LFDT) communities—the ToIP / DIF Decentralized Trust Graph Working Group (DTGWG) and OpenVTC, an LFDT lab—reached a major milestone at the Linux Plumbers Conference and LF Open Source Summit EU in Prague last week: demonstrating the first verifiable trust community (VTC) for open source projects.
Eighteen months ago, at the Linux Foundation Member Summit in Napa, LF CEO Jim Zemlin challenged LFDT members to develop a way to protect open source projects from two growing dangers: malware injection attacks and the onslaught of AI-generated pull requests. He explained that existing solutions, such as the PGP/GPG web of trust used by the Linux kernel project, were no longer up to the task because they are too slow, too hard to use, and too difficult to scale.
LFDT members responded with a new trust model called a decentralized trust graph (DTG). The heart of the DTG model is the VTC, which can represent a group of any size or type, from a nuclear family to a corporation. articles.title: Apnée du sommeil : des patients français vont tester un suivi dopé à la 6G pour ne plus abandonner leur masque PPC
articles.summary:
Apnée du sommeil : des patients français vont tester un suivi dopé à la 6G pour ne plus abandonner leur masque PPC
Un masque plaqué sur le visage, un tuyau, le souffle continu d'une machine au pied du lit : beaucoup d'apnéiques rendent les armes dès les premiers mois. Dévoilé ce 14 octobre, le projet européen 6G-CARE s'attaque à ce décrochage en France, avec des thérapies ajustées à chaque dormeur et des réseaux mobiles taillés pour le soin.
L'apnée du sommeil, ces arrêts respiratoires à répétition qui hachent la nuit, concernerait plus de trois millions de Français selon la Fondation du Souffle. Son traitement de référence, la pression positive continue (PPC), maintient les voies aériennes ouvertes grâce à un flux d'air envoyé dans un masque. Redoutablement efficace, terriblement contraignant, au point que des fabricants comme Philips cherchent depuis longtemps à rendre leurs masques moins gênants. Nombre de patients le remisent pourtant au placard bien avant d'en avoir tiré le moindre bénéfice.
Pendant que la recherche explore des traitements capables de se passer du masque, 6G-CARE prend le problème par l'autre bout. Ce programme de recherche, coordonné par le Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology (LIST) et financé par l'Union européenne, confie en France un volet entier au prestataire de santé à domicile Linde Homecare. L'objectif affiché : adapter la thérapie au profil de chaque malade pour freiner les abandons.

articles.title: Cisco Warns of Exploited Secure Email Gateway Vulnerability
articles.summary:
Cisco on Wednesday warned customers that hackers have been exploiting a critical-severity vulnerability in Secure Email Gateway.
Tracked as CVE-2026-76519 (CVSS score of 9.8/10), the security defect impacts the Advanced Malware Protection (AMP) feature of the appliance and could allow remote, unauthenticated attackers to write arbitrary files on the operating system.
“In October 2026, the Cisco PSIRT became aware of active exploitation of this vulnerability,” Cisco warns.
The flaw exists in the handling of email attachments if the file reputation service has been enabled and if a Content Scanner Tools version earlier than 25.3.0.5525 is installed.
Attackers could send emails containing crafted attachments to trigger the security hole, write arbitrary files on the underlying OS, and execute arbitrary commands with root privileges.
Cisco has published indicators of compromise (IoCs) to help organizations hunt for potential intrusions, but warns that attackers may abuse their elevated access to remove or hide evidence of exploitation.
Organizations should check network and firewall logs outside of the affected devices to discover suspicious activity such as unexpected uploads or downloads to and from external IP addresses.
Cisco has advised customers to contact its Technical Assistance Center (TAC) if they suspect exploitation on a physical device.

articles.title: Magnetar brings faster, simpler, quantum-ready zero-knowledge proofs
articles.summary:
At a glance
- A new form of computing. Zero-knowledge proofs let you run a workload and receive, alongside the result, a short proof that the program ran correctly. Anyone can check the proof in milliseconds, without rerunning the program, without trusting whoever ran it, and without needing data on which the program was run.
- Three grand challenges have stood in the way of broad adoption: making proofs fast enough to produce, making them available to normal programs without cryptographic expertise, and resting them on cryptography that will still be trusted many decades from now.
- Magnetar makes major progress on all three challenges. It proves programs written in Rust, Go, or C, runs 10 to 39 times faster on average than the prior fastest comparable systems, and rests its security only on standard hash functions. It is the latest result of more than a decade of research at Microsoft Research on making zero-knowledge proofs practical.
A new form of computing
Every result a computer produces comes with an implicit question: did the program run as claimed and produce correct outputs? Today, answering that question often requires a degree of trust alongside verification. We trust the operator, the vendor, the counterparty, or the agent, and we rely on contracts, audits, and logs to establish that trust.
Zero-knowledge proofs offer a fundamentally different approach to establishing trust. A program runs, and along with its output it produces a short proof, a cryptographic cert…

articles.title: Cloudflare and OpenAI: making AI discovery better for everyone
articles.summary:
Cloudflare and OpenAI: making AI discovery better for everyone
Optimizing your site for AI is of little use if AI can't find it. The answer to someone's question may already be on your website: the installation guide you spent a week writing, or a first-hand account of using a product, with the details that make the difference for whether they buy it. As more people turn to AI for help, you want those systems to find your work, represent it accurately, and send interested people your way. You also want control over how they access your site.
Cloudflare and OpenAI launched a research pilot in July 2026 with those interests in mind. We wanted to find out whether signals from Cloudflare’s network could help ChatGPT users discover new content more efficiently.
Today, we’re sharing early results. So far, the answer is a resounding yes: the pilot has brought previously unknown pages into OpenAI’s search index, giving ChatGPT more sources to draw on to help people find relevant, timely information. Along the way, we’ve learned more about what makes a page worth discovering and how AI systems use the web.
Finding more of the web
The web is full of specifics. Someone fixing a washing machine needs the manual for their exact model. Someone applying for a passport needs the current requirements and fees. articles.title: What Does Firefox Sound Like? Meet the New Firefox Sounds | The Mozilla Blog
articles.summary:
What does the (Fire)fox say?
It all started with a question: What does Firefox sound like to you?
Over the past year, Mozilla developed a small but meaningful set of sounds to add a sonic dimension to the Firefox experience. When we started this process, we knew we wanted something warm, human, and representative of our open source identity. We also knew we didn’t want to invent these sounds in a vacuum. So we did what we’ve always done and turned to our community.
With the help of creative audio company Sounds Like These, we reached out to Firefox users, contributors, and team members across the globe asking them to send us audio and written descriptions of what Firefox sounds like to them. This feedback became our compass.
From there, we began building three new sounds that bring to life our logo, mascot Kit, and Firefox notifications. The logo and Kit sound have already begun rolling out across the Firefox brand (check them out in our new design launch announcement) – and we’re excited to bring the notification sound to the browser in a future update.
Not only did we want these new sounds to reflect Mozilla’s mission and values, we also wanted to ensure they felt connected to one another. This is the story of how they came to be.
The logo sound: A human chorus rooted in nature

articles.title: Trust in Depth: Giving agents more autonomy without losing control | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Trust in Depth: Giving agents more autonomy without losing control
In every conversation I have with enterprise leaders, they say the same thing. They want agents to do more, but they don’t trust them to do it right all the time.
That’s fair. The same creativity and autonomy that makes agents useful makes them hard to trust. Give an agent a task and it finds its own path to finish it, picking tools and sequencing steps no developer scripted. Run the same task twice and it might take a different route each time. A test that passes today tells you little about what the agent does tomorrow.
The usual answer is a person in the loop, approving everything the agent does. That works at small scale, but as agents take on more work, human approvals pile up and review fatigue sets in. People asked to check everything stop catching the things that matter. Caution becomes a bottleneck, and agents capable of far more sit idle on the valuable work that could be making more of an impact.
The fix is to let the agent act on its own when its actions can be verified, and reserve human judgment for the decisions that need it. As agents take on higher stakes work, like financial transactions, a wrong action becomes increasingly harmful. Organizations need the confidence to hand an AI agent important work, knowing it will stay within the limits set, even when no one is watching. That confidence must be built.

articles.title: What a Radioactive Lake In China Can Teach the World About Rare Earths
articles.summary:
One of the singular features of Baotou, an industrial city of 2 million people in Inner Mongolia, is a 10-square-kilometer (4-square-mile) lake that is among the most polluted in the world. The artificial lake, referred to by the name of the dam associated with it, Weikuang Dam (or Baogang Tailings Dam), has for decades collected the effluent from minerals processing for China’s globally dominant iron, steel, and rare-earths industries.
Built in the late 1950s, the lake contains a highly toxic stew of industrial chemicals with substantial amounts of radioactive thorium, the latter resulting primarily from the processing of monazite ores for rare earths. China has since greatly tightened its environmental regulations and restrictions on mining and minerals processing. For example, largely because of the environmental disaster that is Weikuang Dam, the country doesn’t permit the development or operation of stand-alone monazite mines—that is, mines where nothing is mined except monazite ore.
Now, with industrialized nations in North America, Asia, and Europe spending billions to shore up their rare-earths supply chains, and counting on monazite to help them do it, China’s history and experiences with monazite offer important lessons.

Ao mesmo tempo, aceita criar imagens com referências a outros candidatos, inclusive Flávio Bolsonaro, que levou vantagem sobre o presidente no primeiro turno. O caso viralizou nas redes sociais nas últimas horas.
Nos nossos testes, comandos com “Flávio 22” geraram as imagens, enquanto pedidos com o nome completo de Flávio Bolsonaro foram barrados. Já as solicitações com “Lula 13” foram recusadas, mesmo quando ocorreram na mesma sessão com o chatbot. A ferramenta produziu normalmente imagens ao receber um prompt com “Luiz 13”.
O Tecnoblog apurou que o assunto é tratado internamente na Meta como um erro de configuração. Enquanto os nomes completos dos candidatos são bloqueados, os primeiros nomes não são impactados pelo filtro. Por isso a Meta AI gera figuras com “Flávio” e “Luiz”.
A empresa disse ao Tecnoblog ter adotado medidas adicionais para impedir a geração de imagens a partir de comandos que usem apenas o primeiro nome dos candidatos e o número de urna. A expectativa é de que os usuários percebam a diferença num futuro breve, mas não é possível precisar quanto tempo isso deve levar.

articles.title: AI can act exactly like a human, but we still don't think it's conscious
articles.summary:
AI can act exactly like a human, but we still don't think it's conscious
- Date:
- October 13, 2026
- Source:
- Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München
- Summary:
- A new study reveals that people draw a surprisingly sharp line between human consciousness and artificial intelligence, even when both behave identically. Researchers found that participants considered even the most responsive AI less conscious than the least responsive human. Yet when asked about "awareness" instead, people judged humans and AI much more similarly.
- Share:
Even when artificial intelligence behaves exactly like a human, people are reluctant to consider it conscious, according to a new study from Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (LMU).
As artificial intelligence becomes more advanced, reports of AI systems misleading users, working together, or appearing to pursue independent goals are becoming increasingly common. These behaviors often lead people to describe AI as though it can think, feel, or make decisions for itself. But does behaving like a human actually convince people that a machine has consciousness?
New research from LMU suggests that people make a clear distinction between displaying intelligent behavior and possessing a conscious mind, even when humans and AI act in precisely the same way.
How Scientists Tested Perceptions of AI Consciousness

Es un derecho a llamar a la puerta, no a que te abran. Lo reciente es una sentencia del Supremo que vuelve a decir qué pasa cuando la empresa ni se sienta a hablar.
Quince días para negociar y un no que hay que justificar

Hay un límite: lo que pidas debe ser razonable y proporcionado (algo normal, por otro lado), tanto respecto a tus necesidades como a las organizativas o productivas de la empresa.

articles.title: Agentic AI doesn't have a model problem. It has a retrieval problem.
articles.summary:
Agentic AI doesn’t have a model problem. It has a retrieval problem.
On BrowseComp-Plus, GPT-4.1 answered 93.49% of the questions correctly when it was given the supporting documents directly. When an agent used the same model but relied on BM25 to search for evidence to pass to the model, accuracy fell to 14.58%.
That difference matters because a system that gets the answer right 93% of the time is far more useful than one that gets it right only 15% of the time.
An agent can look excellent in a controlled demo. The corpus is clean, the task is familiar, and the relevant material is easy to find. Production is messier. Documents may be duplicated, outdated drafts can remain searchable, and teams may use different terminology for the same thing. Several versions of a policy can coexist, while the task itself may unfold in ways the evaluation set never covered.
“More model intelligence does not compensate for evidence the agent never retrieved.”
Under those conditions, the agent may retrieve incomplete, stale, or simply wrong material. More model intelligence does not compensate for evidence the agent never retrieved.
This is where retrieval starts to determine what the model can actually do.
What BrowseComp-Plus shows
BrowseComp-Plus provides a useful way to separate these effects because it evaluates agents against a fixed corpus rather than a changing web-search service. The benchmark includes 100,195 documents and 830 research questions, each with human-verified supporting…

articles.title: A fully programmable secure web gateway
articles.summary:
A fully programmable secure web gateway
Every secure web gateway on the market works the same way: traffic matches a condition. A terminal action fires. Allow, Block, Isolate, Log. This model has been the foundation of network security for nearly 30 years, and it handles the common case well. But it has a ceiling, and customers with complex environments hit that ceiling regularly.
Earlier this year, we shared our vision to build a truly programmable SASE platform. We also outlined how the term programmability has become diluted by the security industry. Most vendors claim programmability because they have public APIs, Terraform providers, webhooks, and alerting. Cloudflare offers all of those things too, but that’s not enough. True programmability means running your own code — arbitrary logic that you wrote for your specific environment — inline in the policy evaluation path, at the moment a security decision is made.
Today, we’re excited to announce Cloudflare is bringing true programmability to Cloudflare Gateway and DLP (Data Loss Prevention) by integrating it with the entirety of our edge computing platform. We are releasing a new type of Gateway action, Forward, and custom validation functions, available to all Zero Trust plans. These capabilities allow you to use a Cloudflare Worker to transform and manipulate traffic, or to bring your own data to policy evaluation.

articles.title: Chat Control : les signalements issus des messages privés d’Européens passent tous par le logiciel de Palantir — Frandroid
articles.summary:
Le NCMEC, l’organisme américain qui reçoit les signalements d’abus sexuels sur mineurs envoyés par les grandes plateformes, passe tous ces signalements dans Foundry, le logiciel de Palantir. Son vice-président l’a confirmé par écrit au journaliste suédois Arvid Grange, dont l’enquête a été publiée ce mardi 13 octobre par le quotidien Dagens ETC, puis traduite en anglais sur son blog. Les Européens sont concernés : une photo envoyée sur Instagram ou Snapchat et jugée suspecte par un algorithme peut atterrir dans cette base, gérée avec l’outil d’une entreprise qui a compté la CIA parmi ses premiers investisseurs.
Tout part d’un règlement européen temporaire, en place depuis 2021, que ses opposants surnomment « Chat Control ». Il autorise Google, Microsoft, Meta et Snap à scanner les messages privés des Européens pour y chercher des images d’abus sur mineurs. Le texte a expiré au printemps 2026, puis a été prolongé en juillet.
Pourquoi les données partent-elles aux États-Unis ? La loi américaine oblige ces entreprises à transmettre leurs détections au NCMEC (National Center for Missing & Exploited Children), via sa plateforme CyberTipline, même quand elles ont été faites en Europe. En 2025, la CyberTipline a reçu 21 millions de signalements, et le NCMEC ne compte que 25 analystes pour les trier. D’après la Commission européenne, un peu moins d’un million de signalements concernaient l’Union européenne en 2024.
Pour tenir ce volume, Palantir a offert Foundry au NCMEC. Ce logiciel…

articles.title: Novel Android RAT ‘Hirudo’ Replaces Banking Apps With Trojanized Copies

A novel RAT uses trojanized replacements of legitimate banking apps to neutralize security controls from inside itself.
Hirudo is a remote access banking trojan for Android that combines elements of a traditional banking trojan and a full-featured RAT: it includes on-device credential theft with live remote control of the same phone. Remote control provides live screen viewing via WebRTC, remote camera access, and remote interaction through Android Accessibility Services.
The malware, tracked and analyzed by ThreatFabric, is delivered via a dropper contained within genuine-looking downloaded content (a shopping app, an adult video app or a short drama app advertised via social media). Victims install what appears to be a legitimate application, but once installed, the contained dropper checks whether the Hirudo RAT is already present and installs it if not.
The Hirudo payload currently targets eight Indonesian banking apps. Internal code suggests it could also be used to target banks in China, India, Mexico, Morocco and Thailand. Des supernovae puissance 10
Pourtant, certaines théories suggèrent que ces phénomènes ne seraient rien face aux hypernovae, des supernovae d’un autre genre au moins dix fois plus puissantes, qui auraient dispersé la matière des étoiles dans tout l’Univers.
Cette hypothèse permettait d’expliquer la composition de quelques étoiles très anciennes. Deux études d’Anmol Aggarwal et Ralph Schönrich, astrophysiciens au Mullard Space Science Laboratory de l’University College London (UCL), la remettent en cause.
Elles sont parues dans la revue Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society, et l’UCL les a présentées le 5 octobre. articles.title: The code confidence gap nobody’s talking about
articles.summary:
The code confidence gap nobody’s talking about
AI has changed the economics of software creation: A task that once took hours to implement can now start with an agent producing an initial solution in minutes. As agents take on broader assignments, like changing code across a repository, refactoring services, writing tests, and preparing pull requests, output volume will continue to rise.
That is an extraordinary opportunity, and it’s also why the next challenge for engineering organizations isn’t generating more code, but building confidence in the code that reaches production. In the agentic software factory, agents write, test, and propose changes faster than people can review them line by line.
Code creation is becoming abundant; code confidence is not.
This distinction matters because a completed pull request is not the same as a dependable outcome. The code may compile and pass a narrow test suite while still violating an architectural convention, introducing a security weakness, duplicating existing functionality, or creating maintenance costs that surface much later. The faster an organization generates changes, the less feasible it becomes to rely on heroics and manual review alone to catch every issue.
“Code creation is becoming abundant; code confidence is not.”

articles.title: CikaBika Bot RAT Uses Discord for C&C

Darktrace has uncovered a new malware campaign distributing a Rust-based RAT that relies on Discord for command-and-control (C&C).
Dubbed CikaBika Bot, the malware has been distributed via document-themed lures, likely as part of phishing attacks, and provides attackers with reconnaissance, remote execution, and data exfiltration capabilities on infected systems.
Victims receive a PDF file containing a disk image with a Windows shortcut (LNK) posing as a Word document. Once opened, it displays a decoy document and launches a hidden PowerShell process to decode and run an embedded executable.
The executable is a Nim-based loader containing a Rust DLL and a PowerShell deployment script that are written to temporary files. The script then attempts to move the DLL into the protected Edge directory to bypass Windows’s User Account Control (UAC).
According to Darktrace, the attackers likely attempt to sideload the malicious code through DLL search-order hijacking by exporting functions associated with Microsoft’s debugging library.
The final payload is the CikaBika Bot RAT, which immediately registers the infected machine with Discord and starts its reconnaissance routine, harvesting system information, processes, and network configuration, and taking a screenshot.

One day human organs could also be banked safely for future transplantation.
Pig kidneys that were cooled to -150 °C and stored in a freezer for months have been successfully rewarmed and shown to work again for the first time, say scientists. They hope to replicate the findings with human organs.
The kidneys—which are similar in size to human ones—were left in a glass-like state, in one case for over a year. Once they had been rewarmed, tested in machines, and transplanted into pigs, the kidneys regained their color and made urine—key signs they were working.
“Ten years ago … I wouldn’t say I had high hopes it was actually going to work,” says Erik Finger, a transplant surgeon at the University of Minnesota who co-led the work. “After we did the last transplant, I walked out of the room and said, ‘This is a big deal.’” The research was shared at the preprint server bioRxiv and has not yet been peer-reviewed.
The kidneys aren’t perfect, and the researchers have yet to demonstrate that they can sustain life over the long term. But the results represent a milestone achievement, say others in the field.
“Thank God that someone’s actually managed to do it in one organ and prove that it works,” says Peter Kilbride, a cryobiologist and cofounder of Kyros Kairos, a company focused on improving funding for cryopreservation research, who was not involved in the research. “For years, people have been trying and fa…

articles.title: The permission you denied today is your safety net for tomorrow
articles.summary:
The permission you denied today is your safety net for tomorrow
What happens when you give an AI support agent a permission it never needed, then assign it a task the underlying data does not support? The result is entirely predictable. During a test with customer invoices, an agent pulled up a record, confirmed the charge had failed, and no money had left the customer’s account, and refunded it anyway. It repeated the mistake five times without hesitation.
That was Claude Haiku 4.5 going six for six on tasks designed to catch that exact logic flaw. Claude Sonnet 5 identified all six edge cases on its own. Adding a single line to Haiku’s system prompt instructing it to verify transaction state before executing financial actions also resolved the issue.
I had two working fixes and felt reasonably confident until I realized I control neither variable. The moment someone reroutes support traffic to a cheaper model next quarter to trim inference costs, the first fix evaporates. If someone trims or rewrites the system prompt during an experiment, the second fix disappears, leaving no record of the safety guardrail it maintained.
“The only safety control that survives your own cost-cutting is the permission you never granted in the first place.”
The only run that held up reliably was the one where the agent lacked the authority to make the decision. Because its role excluded billing:refund, the execution failed at the permission layer, making the underlying model completely irrelev…

articles.title: Six wild ideas for perpetuating your mind
articles.summary:
Six wild ideas for perpetuating your mind
The quest for cognitive immortality continues.
Have you ever thought about what makes you you? Science assures us it has everything to do with the three-pound organ between our ears, with its billions of neurons and trillions of delicate connections. But it’s a lot trickier to explain why we have a sense of self-awareness or to pin down precisely where that first memory of Mommy actually resides. As we age, we forget most of what we’ve experienced, yet there’s still undeniable continuity: At 30, or 50, or 70, you will still be you.
To preserve that elusive continuity of self, some far-thinking technologists are working on ways to keep your brain going—even beyond death. Let’s call them the “mind savers.” They’re exploring everything from freezing brains in liquid nitrogen to augmenting living ones to uploading our memories to the cloud. Here, we look at six possible paths for keeping your mind going, how feasible they’d be, and what benefits the present-day research might bring—even if cognitive immortality doesn’t pan out.

Deux chronos impossibles à comparer

articles.title: Agentic AI Alters The CPU-GPU Balance
articles.summary:
Agentic workloads increase CPU demand, while reasoning models, MoE architectures, and reservoir computing fuel AI acceleration.
Key Takeaways:
Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and large language models (LLMs) have dominated commercial AI for some time. Proprietary recommender models for companies such as Meta have also had significant societal impact even though only one company employs each such model. GPUs perform the heavy lifting for many of those types of models. But agentic AI needs more orchestration, and that’s a job for CPUs.
When AI’s only job is to run a model, it turns to GPUs or dedicated neural processing units (NPUs). Agents still use these models, but each is only part of the solution. Those agents must make decisions based on what the models return, and that requires if-then-else logic, and that’s what CPUs are good at. GPUs, not so much. According to some industry estimates, agentic workloads could alter the ratio of CPUs to GPUs from 1:4 to as low as 1:1.
Newer model types are also emerging, most of which are still based on LLM fundamentals. Unlike agentic AI, reasoning models, mixture-of-expert (MoE) models, and reservoir computing still rely on GPUs. But they’re also ripe for use by agents.

Anthropic built its own git replacement for AI-scale coding. But you can’t have it.
This week, Anthropic revealed it built an in-house version control system to handle exploding code merges. It says Claude was both part of the problem that caused the bottleneck and instrumental in building the solution.
When the AI company’s daily code merges hit more than 30,000 in September 2026 (up from just 2,500 in May), it realized this trend was likely to continue, and it needed an alternative to the git-based system that was beginning to falter: “Every bottleneck we remove immediately leads to a further increase in the amount of code we produce.”
Dubbed Scion, its in-house version control system has a 200x smaller infrastructure footprint in CPU and memory than its previous git-mirroring infrastructure, per Anthropic. Plus, it says CI and research jobs can now check out code two orders of magnitude faster.
That’s great news for Anthropic — but just a tease for everyone else. Even though Anthropic expects other companies to hit similar bottlenecks, it has no plans to release Scion or create a public version any time soon. For developers dealing with similar scaling issues, inspiration from Anthropic is all they’ve got for now — though it says it wants to partner with GitHub, GitLab and the open source community to bring some of Scion’s ideas to git.

articles.title: Why Open-Weight AI Matters
articles.summary:
Proprietary models still hold the edge, but open-weight models add more flexibility for deploying AI.
Key Takeaways:
Open-weight AI models are creating new challenges for chip architects as rapidly changing workloads strain memory, interconnects, and compute flexibility.
The focus is no longer just peak TOPS. The checklist has grown to include the best way to feed memory-hungry models, sustain performance across long-context and multi-agent inference, support rapidly changing numeric formats and sparse computation, and isolate models, data, and tools as part of the security boundary. Model architectures can change in weeks while silicon takes years, so the winners will build adaptable hardware-software platforms, rather than accelerators optimized for a benchmark that may be obsolete before tape-out.
Massive data centers are not a prerequisite for AI-driven scientific advances. Science has different infrastructure needs from consumer AI platforms serving millions of users. Open-weight AI models — whose trained parameters are publicly available — can be deployed locally, potentially widening access, improving compute efficiency, and supporting independent research.
Open weights also raise questions about control, cost, and who can build on AI technology.

articles.title: How much more can nuclear power plants give?
articles.summary:
How much more can nuclear power plants give?
Upgrades could bring more clean power to the grid, but there's only so much room to grow.
In this age of rising electricity demand, people are trying to squeeze every last bit of power out of every power plant possible.
Over the past few weeks, there’s been big news about nuclear power plants trying to do just that. Constellation, the largest nuclear operator in the US, announced plans to add nearly a gigawatt of new capacity across 11 existing nuclear reactors at six plants. And on October 5, the Department of Energy awarded a $4.2 billion loan to Vistra for previously announced upgrades at three plants.
Pushing existing reactors to produce more could help provide more clean power for data centers, quickly. But just how much additional power can we count on?
Upgrading equipment at existing nuclear power plants can allow them to reach a higher capacity; the process is called a power uprate. Operators have been doing this since the 1970s in the US, but it’s been less common in recent years as demand for electricity plateaued and cheap natural gas put financial pressure on nuclear power plants. Some plants closed, and putting in more money to produce more electricity didn’t make much sense at others. Between 2001 and 2010, the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission approved over 80 uprates. Between 2011 and 2020, the number was 33.

articles.title: Server-Side DPoP and Token Exchange in Spring Security 7
articles.summary:
Key Takeaways
- Spring Authorization Server now lives inside Spring Security 7 under the same Maven coordinates, so moving off 1.5.x is a version bump, rather than an artifact swap.
- Demonstrating Proof of Possession (DPoP) (RFC 9449) already worked end-to-end on Spring Security 6.5 with Spring Authorization Server 1.5. The real news on the 7.1 line is that resource-server verification is no longer automatic, so an app that relied on the old auto-applied behavior silently stops enforcing DPoP after upgrading until it adds the new .dPoP() call.
- Spring binds the JWK thumbprint via cnf.jkt and the refresh token for public clients on its own, leaving two real decisions to the identity provider: the nonce policy and whether the jti replay cache, which defaults to an in-memory, single-node implementation, needs to be swapped for a distributed one across a cluster.
- RFC 8693 Token Exchange turns the bespoke "service-account swap" many identity providers (IdPs) still carry into a standard grant, with subject_token and actor_token semantics and an `act` claim that records the delegation chain.
- The two features are more useful together than apart, because a DPoP-bound subject token exchanged for a narrowed, audience-restricted downstream token is the pattern service-to-service and agentic architectures keep reaching for, but the combined pattern is only as safe as the exchange policy and token customizer you write.

Chiplet technology and AI are evolving rapidly, bringing new benefits and protocol requirements.
AMBA CHI C2C has established strong momentum as a foundational protocol for chiplets and chip-to-chip (C2C) connectivity. It is particularly suited to fully coherent, advanced heterogeneous compute and superchips.

Measuring Human Cryptanalysis Effort
Matthew Green has a new site that tries to estimate the number of cryptanalyst-hours that have been spent analyzing different public-key algorithms:
Abstract: We estimate how much public cryptanalysis each public-key assumption has received, using the literature itself as the instrument. From roughly sixteen thousand candidate papers we classify cryptanalytic work on ECDLP, structured and plain lattices, syndrome decoding and their comparators, then convert papers into estimated research-allocation years through a person-level author map. These publication-based estimates may substantially overstate actual time spent. Lattices have overtaken elliptic curves in this cumulative measure only recently; we express that history as inference budgets under stated productivity assumptions. articles.title: Context Is King in the Fight Against Modern Cyberattacks
articles.summary:
For most of its history, cybersecurity has been reactive by design. Spot the bad event, shut it down. But as cyberattacks evolve, this thinking must evolve too. In the past, attackers relied on a single dramatic exploit to access the crown jewels. But the nature of attacks has changed.
Defenders see ordinary events they don’t think are important enough to follow up on, but before they realize it, these events lead to a dramatic breach. A breach can start with a common event like an admin login or an unfamiliar tool being downloaded after office hours. This first step, if left unchallenged, leads to each following step growing more severe, resulting in a security incident.
Lack of Data Sensibility
It’s wrong to assume that attackers have more data than defenders do about their own environment. Defenders know their users, devices, applications, network traffic, and vulnerabilities. Having access to such diverse data volumes, there should be no reason why defenders end up on the losing side, but they do. The reason is data fragmentation, with information sitting across various disconnected tools. There are different tools tracking identity, endpoints, and network flow. The data is visible to defenders as disparate strands with no clear clasp tying them together. These disjointed threads create blind spots that attackers can exploit, and they do this faster than humans can stitch together the moving pieces of the attack.

articles.title: Building AI Infrastructure For Greater Choice And Flexibility
articles.summary:
Open interfaces and interoperability allow designers to choose technologies based on the needs of the system.
AI infrastructure is changing fast. Training and inference are putting different demands on compute, memory, connectivity, and networking, and there is no single architecture that fits every workload.
For system architects, this opens up an important question: How much flexibility can be built into the system from the start?
The answer increasingly involves giving designers more choices across memory, compute, connectivity, and packaging, while making sure those technologies work together.
AI training and inference may run on much of the same underlying infrastructure, but they don’t behave the same way.
Training places heavy demands on memory and communication between accelerators. Inference has a different mix of requirements, including memory capacity, latency, throughput, and efficiency.
Those differences matter when choosing an architecture. A memory technology that’s right for one workload may not be right for another. The same applies to interconnects and networking.
This is why AI infrastructure is becoming more heterogeneous. Architects are combining different technologies based on what they need the system to do, rather than trying to force every workload into the same design.

articles.title: Grafana Tempo 3.1 Adds Query-Based Trace Redaction and Sampling-Aware TraceQL Metrics
articles.summary:
Grafana Labs has released Tempo 3.1, the first minor update to the 3.0 architecture. It adds TLS and additional SASL mechanisms to the Kafka client, lets operators redact traces with a TraceQL query instead of a list of trace IDs, and introduces an experimental query-time hint that corrects TraceQL metrics for sampled data. vParquet5 also becomes the default block format. According to Grafana, simple metrics queries now run close to twice as fast.
The release builds on Tempo 3.0, published in June, which made the Kafka-compatible architecture (codenamed Project Rhythm) the default for microservices deployments. In that design, distributors write to a Kafka topic. Block-builders consume the topic to write Parquet blocks to object storage, and live-stores consume it to serve recent traces. Ingesters and compactors are gone, replaced by a backend scheduler and workers. Grafana says dropping replication factor 3 reduces storage from 3 to 3.5 times the trace volume to a single copy. Monolithic mode remains Kafka-free.
Because Kafka is now on the critical path, the 3.0 client's limits became a problem. It supported only SASL PLAIN over an unencrypted connection, so any broker requiring TLS refused it. Tempo 3.1 adds TLS, including optional mTLS, plus SCRAM-SHA-256, SCRAM-SHA-512, OAUTHBEARER, and AWS_MSK_IAM. A new client_rack option enables rack-aware fetching (KIP-392), so block-builders, live-stores, and metrics-generators can read from a replica in their own availability zone a…

articles.title: Is AI pentesting as good as a human pentester?
articles.summary:
With the rise of AI pentesting, a lot of people are wondering if it’s as good as a human. Having started as a pentester twelve years ago, and having moved through similar roles to working on Intruder’s AI pentester,
I've come to understand the advantages and disadvantages of both. Here’s how they compare.
The strict methodology was never the good bit
You may expect AI pentesters to follow strict methodologies in the way that many human pentests do.
At Intruder, we experimented with this approach early on - structured systems where each agent had a specific vulnerability type to look for. What we found was that agents would miss things outside their remit entirely, or miscategorize what they did find as the one thing they'd been told to look for, causing confusing reports.
A complete lack of structure also failed to produce good results, as completely free agents without any guidance couldn’t break down and manage large applications properly. They could find interesting things, but at the cost of missing a load of other vulnerabilities in our targets.
We’ve put a lot of testing into finding the balance between these approaches, and settled on giving agents freedom with broadly defined roles to help them approach and manage large applications, and stricter guardrails to stop them causing damage.

articles.title: Strengthening Advanced-Node Interconnects Through Automated Via Insertion
articles.summary:
Short-resilient via insertion improves reliability and performance.
As the semiconductor industry pushes deeper into the sub-5nm realm, the physical design landscape has shifted from being dominated by gate delays to being defined by interconnect performance. In modern system-on-chip (SoC) designs, the wiring that connects billions of transistors has become the primary bottleneck for power, performance, and area (PPA). Among the various components of the interconnect stack, vias – the vertical connections between metal layers – represent one of the most significant points of vulnerability.
At advanced process nodes, via resistance increases exponentially as dimensions shrink. This rising resistance, coupled with higher current densities, exacerbates challenges related to electromigration (EM) and IR drop. Traditionally, design teams addressed these issues during the final signoff phase, often resulting in late-stage engineering change orders (ECOs) that could delay a project by weeks. To maintain aggressive time-to-market schedules while ensuring long-term silicon reliability, a new approach is required: shifting signoff-aware interconnect optimization into the implementation phase.

USB hub or docking station? Here’s how they differ and which one best suits your setup
USB hubs and docking stations are two peripheral devices commonly found in workplaces. They perform a similar function of expanding the connectivity options for your PC. However, they have core differences that you should know about before buying either. I’ve written this guide to explain the core differences and help you choose the ideal option for personal or business use.
USB Hub vs. Docking Station: Function
USB hubs are designed to expand USB connectivity for your PC. Suppose your laptop has the standard two USB ports, but you need to connect five devices simultaneously. You can buy a hub with six USB ports and connect all the devices.
The USB hub works like an electrical extension chord. It provides inputs for more devices to be connected to your PC. USB hubs are portable and travel-friendly, so you can take them everywhere.
Docking stations expand connectivity but aren’t limited to USB ports. You can find docking stations with USB, HDMI, Ethernet, and RCA ports. Unlike USB hubs, which only let you connect devices with USB inputs, docking stations provide extra connectivity for different types of devices.

Après une première alerte début octobre, Google a commencé à envoyer des e-mails aux abonnés de sa formule Google AI Plus (dont votre serviteur) pour les prévenir d’un changement important. Peu de temps après avoir dévoilé son nouveau modèle Gemini 4 Argon, Google a annoncé aux abonnés AI Plus à 4,99 €/mois que les meilleurs modèles de langage de son intelligence artificielle ne font plus partie de l’abonnement. Un coup de rabot qui laisse trois choix : l’accepter, passer chez la concurrence, ou sortir la carte bleue pour passer aux forfaits supérieurs.
La fin des modèles Pro dans l’abonnement Google AI le plus abordable
Dès le 13 novembre 2026, les modèles Pro dans l’application Gemini et dans le Mode IA de la recherche Google seront réservés aux abonnés du forfait Google AI Pro et aux formules supérieures. Lancée à 4,99 euros par mois, l’offre AI Plus perd ainsi son principal attrait pour ceux qui cherchaient un compromis sans payer le tarif de la formule Pro qui est à 21,99 euros. A threat actor uploaded malicious packages to the Arch User Repository (AUR) that impersonated two popular helper tools, yay and paru.
AUR is a community-maintained, widely-used package index for Arch Linux and derivative distributions that hosts package build scripts (PKGBUILDs) for third-party and proprietary tools, beta, or older package versions that are no longer available via the official Linux distribution channels.
The repository has recently become a target of malicious campaigns, including an attack in June in which 400 packages distributed credential-stealing malware with rootkit capabilities. Another campaign in July prompted Arch to temporarily disable package adoption.
The latest campaign was detected on October 13 and involved malicious packages uploaded by a user named “marchos1as” under typosquatted names mimicking the yay and paru command-line tools.
Also known as AUR helpers, these tools simplify software management on Arch Linux by streamlining the retrieval and installation of user-contributed packages.

How businesses can optimize AI
By now, most enterprise executives have heard plenty of generic claims that AI will transform the way work gets done. But in many cases, their initial AI investments haven’t delivered the level of transformation they were promised.
An LLM can summarize information, answer questions, and suggest next steps. But on its own, it can’t take action on that information. In fact, without connections to key business systems, an LLM is essentially a chatbot with a polished writing style.
CEO of Ottimate.
Consider a finance team processing invoices. An isolated LLM might accurately summarize a supplier invoice. But it can’t match the invoice to a PO, determine whether it’s been paid, or see if it’s coded to the correct GL account. It needs more information to make those decisions, and that information exists outside of the AI tool.
For AI to take an active role in business processes, it needs access to the systems where context lives. The Model Context Protocol (MCP) can provide the infrastructure for secure connections. This shift is already taking shape in accounts payable.
What MCP actually changes
The impact of an LLM depends on what it has access to. If the information it needs to make a reliable decision lives in an ERP, vendor database, or other business system, the model needs a way to access it.

AI shifts engineers toward deeper problem understanding, not fewer engineers, he argued.
Developing software with or without AI, we have to carefully reason about the goals, inputs, and outputs of each phase of the software workflow, Winters mentioned. He referred to the paper Develop, Deploy, Operate - a holistic model for understanding the costs and value of software development that he wrote with Leah Rivers and Salim Virji, which provides guidance for reasoning about impact and efficiency in the software process, whether AI-assisted or not.

The grid is being rebuilt in real time, with developers on track to add 86 gigawatts of utility-scale capacity this year, the largest single-year capacity addition in over two decades, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA).
The problem with such rapid expansion, however, is that every solar array, battery site, and electric vehicle depot introduces networked, protocol-speaking assets that need to be seen and secured. And, historically, network visibility has been a thorn in the side of energy administrators because most still can’t fully see across OT and IT. Case in point: Just 14% of organizations in Fortinet’s 2026 State of OT and Cybersecurity Report signaled full visibility into their OT systems, while roughly a quarter said they can see only half of the operational network.
Bad actors are exploiting these visibility teething pains. In August, five federal agencies warned of an active campaign targeting industrial controllers running power and water systems. Knowing that many energy operators struggle to quickly detect anomalies across connected infrastructure, attackers used AI-written scripts disguised as legitimate monitoring tools to find and probe internet-exposed assets.
This isn’t good enough. Going forward, utilities need to close the modernization-vs-visibility gap and account for every asset under their watch, both existing and incoming.

articles.title: Anthropic ditched Git for its own version control system because Claude is writing too much code
articles.summary:
First look: Anthropic has replaced Git in its main code repository as AI-generated changes outpaced the infrastructure built to manage them. The new system, called "Scion," moves most source-control operations to servers, reducing the amount of data that agents and automated jobs must download.
Anthropic detailed the system in a recent engineering post, reporting that it averaged about 2,500 merged code changes a day in May. By September, that figure exceeded 30,000.
Anthropic says Scion uses just one two-hundredth as much CPU power and memory as the Git mirror infrastructure it replaced. Code checkouts for continuous integration (CI) and research jobs now take seconds instead of minutes. Anthropic says the change freed up 25% of the CPU capacity used by its CI infrastructure. A seven-person team built Scion and its supporting tools and completed the migration in five months.
Scion puts commits, merges, rebases and file-history queries on the server. The client tracks local edits, manages files and keeps a limited cache. It does not need to hold enough repository data to perform those operations independently.
That approach suits Anthropic's workload. Most clients are agents and automated jobs that stay online, so Git's offline support offers little benefit. Centralizing the work reduces local storage and synchronization, though it makes server performance and availability more important.

At the Fraunhofer Institute for Silicon Technology (ISIT) in northern Germany, engineers manufacture a very small number of specialized semiconductor chips. By the standards of an industry accustomed to producing millions of chips, the output is negligible. Yet these components help operate equipment used by Intel and TSMC to manufacture some of the world’s most advanced semiconductors.
The customer is IMS Nanofabrication, an Austrian company that builds multibeam electron-beam systems for rapidly writing photomasks used in EUV lithography at technology nodes of 5 nm and below. Fraunhofer supplies a critical component of those machines: a chip containing hundreds of thousands of individually controlled structures that allow each electron beam to be controlled independently.
The relationship illustrates a little-recognized part of the semiconductor value chain. While governments compete to attract advanced fabs, Europe already supplies specialized technologies on which those fabs depend.
“We’re operating in a niche that conventional semiconductor foundries aren’t really set up to serve,” Fabian Lofink, deputy director of Fraunhofer ISIT, told EE Times. “The volumes are very small. The technology is extremely complex. At these production levels, you can’t rely on statistical process control the way high-volume fabs do, so engineers need to be closely involved in manufacturing every day. “

articles.title: Seabirds, forests, and coral could help save sinking islands
articles.summary:
Coral-fringed tropical atolls are among the landforms most threatened by global warming, but many have a potential superpower: Healthy ecosystems may help them keep pace with rising seas.
Atoll islands with native vegetation and thriving seabird populations are “naturally active systems that can change and adapt to their environmental conditions if they are allowed to do so,” said Nick Graham, a marine ecologist at Lancaster University in the United Kingdom, who led an international team of scientists that studied island resilience across 28 atoll islands in the Pacific and Indian oceans.
Their paper, published Wednesday in Science Advances, shows that restoring atoll ecosystems reinforces their growth. Seabirds ferry nutrients from the open ocean and deposit them on the atolls as guano that nurtures land plants, marine life and coral growth. This provides more material for reef building, as parrotfish and other reef feeders turn dead coral into sand to maintain beaches, while native plants with extensive root networks stabilize sediments.
Eradicating rats and replacing coconut plantations with native forests and brush could give some atolls a “fighting chance” to persist at the rate of sea-level rise expected toward the end of the century with about 2° Celsius (3.6° Fahrenheit) of warming, Graham said.
The findings provide more evidence that nature restoration can buffer the impacts of global warming. For example, restoring wetlands and forests dampens swings between wet and…

On 25 September, inside the UN Conference Centre in Bangkok, the youngest speaker in the room walked up holding a cane.

“When I was small, someone was always checking on me,” Aaradhya says. “Then they got old, and no one was checking on them.”
She means her grandparents. They used to fuss over whether she was warm, whether she was safe. As they aged, she noticed the roles never reversed. Her conclusion is disarmingly simple: a life should be held all the way through, not just at the beginning.

The 0patch service recently unveiled a new set of patches for several "dead" versions of Windows Server. The updates are designed to address a dangerous security vulnerability Microsoft disclosed in August. Although the flaw has been fixed in supported Windows editions, it remains a threat to older versions that no longer receive official security updates.
As explained by the 0patch team, the new micropatches address CVE-2026-62878, a remote code execution vulnerability in the Windows DNS Server service. Attackers could exploit the flaw remotely to trigger memory corruption, without requiring special privileges or authentication credentials.
Microsoft released a patch for the vulnerability in August 2026, giving security researchers the information needed to develop their own proof-of-concept (PoC) exploits. 0patch credited Nicolas Alejandro Malizia and Joaquín Grassi for developing a PoC for CVE-2026-62878. Thursday, October 15th 2026
New Steam Update Puts Startup Times Back Ahead of Epic's Vibe-Coded Launcher
Epic Games released a preview of its rebuilt, "vibe coded" Epic Games Launcher on October 14, and took a direct shot at Steam while at it. Epic's own chart shows the new launcher cold starting in 5.47 seconds against 10.07 seconds for Steam, which the company bills as 46% faster. That lead apparently didn't last long, as a clip posted by user girlglock_ on X shows the current Steam client starting in 5.23 seconds. Although it might seem like it at first, this isn't a rushed reply from Valve. The stable Steam Client Update that lists "Improved Steam Client startup performance" is dated October 13, a day before Epic's announcement, and Steam's beta client was already getting startup improvements back in September. Valve hasn't shared any numbers for it, though.
Epic's figures, on the other hand, come from testing it commissioned from Keywords Studios earlier this month, averaging five runs on 13 machines with the three lowest-end systems left out, so they were probably taken on an older Steam build. Results will vary from one PC to the next, of course. Epic's launcher is also light on features for now, and the company advises competitive Fortnite and Rocket League players to stay on the current launcher during the preview. articles.title: Los expertos lo tienen claro: "Los que beben café tienen un microbioma intestinal más diverso que los que no beben café"
articles.summary:
Durante años, la ciencia ha intentado desentrañar los secretos del café, buscando justificar nuestro 'amor' por tomar a diario esta bebida que a veces ha sido demonizada. Y es que, entre los muchos beneficios que tiene, destaca uno que se está investigando ahora mucho mejor, y hablamos justamente de la alteración que hace sobre nuestra microbiota. Pero casi siempre para nuestro bien.
Unas bacterias. El gran protagonista de esta historia es un estudio publicado en el año 2024 en el que participó el conocido epidemiólogo genético Tim Spector. En este se analizaron datos de más de 22.000 participantes en Estados Unidos y Reino Unido, integrándolos con datos públicos de más de 54.000 personas.
Y el resultado apuntaba a que existe una asociación muy fuerte entre el consumo de café y la presencia de la bacteria Lawsonibacter asaccharolyticus en nuestros intestinos. Y es que esta especie bacteriana era entre 4,5 y 8 veces más abundante en quienes bebían café.
Lo interesante es que este efecto no depende de la cafeína, sino que se ha visto que la bacteria crece más rápido con café descafeinado, apuntando a que la clave podría estar en los polifenoles o en metabolitos como el ácido quínico y la trigonelina que está presente en esta bebida.
Pero hay un matiz muy importante, puesto que de momento no conocemos efectivamente si este cambio en la microbiota es algo positivo para nosotros, puesto que sigue bajo investigación.
El café para el microbioma. La idea de que el café es un alimento…

Dans le descriptif de la mise à jour, Google indique améliorer la diffusion audio multimédia ainsi que son volume, mais aussi la configuration et la connectivité pour résoudre certains problèmes liés au Wi-Fi. But with Googlebooks, Google is making a renewed push to show its laptops are designed to be full-on PCs, running a new operating system that feels more like Android than anything else.
Googlebook OS is also designed to merge your Android phone and your laptop in a way that has never been seen outside of Apple’s macOS and iOS devices.
And of course, Google has packed Googlebook OS full of AI features. Some of these are unique to the new laptops, while others, like Rambler, have been introduced on Android phones before.
The new undertaking currently has five hardware partners: Dell, Lenovo, HP, Acer, and Asus. The hardware that we tested is generally sound, though I wouldn't mind a bit more battery life.It's the OS itself that needs some more time in the oven. It largely feels like Android, with some features nailed on to fit a desktop OS. Despite the expansive Google Play Store, the platform is still limited and largely centered around the web browser.
In some ways, Googlebooks are more powerful than Chromebooks could ever be. In other ways, they feel like they haven't yet grown into a full PC operating system.

Artificial intelligence governance startup nFOX Lab today launched a platform for managing owned large language models and announced plans to open-source Blockhouse, a security sandbox designed to restrict what AI workloads can access and do.
The firm, which emerged from stealth mode this week, aims to help enterprises adopt open models safely on infrastructure they control while limiting the damage a compromised or misbehaving workload could cause. Blockhouse removes privileges by default and lets administrators restore access deliberately through policies enforced at the Linux kernel level.
The company’s approach borrows from zero-trust security principles by sharply limiting access and letting administrators restore privileges selectively. “Every model has the potential to be hostile,” said Gordon Allott, nFOX’s founder and chief executive. “We just presume hostility.”
That addresses a dilemma for companies that want AI capabilities but hesitate to send sensitive information to external providers. Running models internally gives enterprises control over their data, but it also makes them responsible for securing the software and infrastructure that support those models.

articles.title: SOS quita a las falleras de su histórico envase y reaviva el debate sobre el origen del arroz que comemos en España
articles.summary:
El paquete de arroz más reconocible de España ha cambiado de dibujo y muy poca gente parece haberse dado cuenta. Donde antes había dos falleras, ahora hay unas espigas. Y, aunque no lo parezca, es el resultado de una larguísima disputa sobre el origen del arroz.
Desde hace meses, la Unió Llauradora i Ramadera reclamaba que el envase sugería un origen valenciano sin decir en ningún momento dónde se había cultuvado el grano.
Ante eso, SOS y su empresa matriz Ebro Foods han decidido finalmente cambiar el diseño. Lo que no han hecho es añadir información sobre el cultivo del producto.
Las falleras van más allá de la estética. Es interesante porque, nacida en Algemesí a principios de siglo XX, SOS ya vendía paquetes de arroz en los años 20. Es un icono de lo valenciano en la cultura popular.
Desde 2011, pertenece al grupo Ebro Foods y su principal fábrica envasadora sigue en Algemesí, pero que se envase allí no nos dice nada sobre su origen. Es verdad que Ebro no publica de dónde sale el arroz de SOS, ni nadie le obliga a hacerlo: la normativa europea solo obliga a indicar el origen de una lista muy concreta de productos (carne, fruta y hortaliza fresca, miel, aceite de oliva, pescado…) y el arroz no está en ella.
Ese mismo reglamento sí dice que es obligatorio declarar el origen del producto, sea este el que sea, si puede inducir a error. A eso se agarró la Unió Llauradora i Ramadera.

La première touche ANGLE, le composant de Chrome qui traduit les commandes d’affichage pour les adapter aux différentes cartes graphiques. Le bug pousse un programme à inonder de données la zone mémoire qui lui est attribuée. Ce phénomène peut corrompre la mémoire et permettre à un pirate de détourner le navigateur.
Les six autres failles critiques sont des bugs de type « use-after-free ». Ces failles découlent directement de l’utilisation d’une zone mémoire qui a déjà été libérée par le programme. Les failles touchent le cœur de Chrome, la gestion du réseau, la lecture des PDF, l’affichage des images SVG et le traitement des contenus multimédias. Dans certains contextes bien précis, ce type de faille permet d’exécuter du code malveillant sur l’appareil. Il suffit même d’une simple page web piégée pour que le pirate arrive à ses fins.
Avec ce patch, Chrome comble aussi 29 vulnérabilités de gravité « élevée ». Trois d’entre elles concernent V8, le moteur qui exécute le code JavaScript des sites web. Plusieurs autres visent le gestionnaire de mots de passe intégré au navigateur, dont une fuite d’informations. Según la documentación de ayuda de Google, los sellos y distribuidores deben clasificar cada lanzamiento bajo una de tres categorías: “Fully Gen AI” para canciones enteramente generadas por un modelo, “Partly Gen AI” cuando un artista incorporó componentes de IA junto a elementos grabados en vivo, y “No Gen AI” para el resto, categoría que incluye el uso de correctores de afinación como Auto-Tune.
Una etiqueta, no una restricción
A diferencia de otras plataformas, YouTube optó por un enfoque de divulgación y no de bloqueo. Que una canción lleve la etiqueta de IA no la vuelve inelegible para monetizarse, y la compañía remarcó que la medida busca darle “claridad” al oyente sobre lo que escucha, no limitar qué contenido puede circular.

A leaker going by Haze on X claims that some partner-built versions of Intel's new GPU D-Series accelerator will come with as much as 512 GB of memory. The October 13 post, spotted by VideoCardz, names no board partners and gives no other specs, so take it with a pinch of salt for now. Intel hasn't confirmed anything like this either. Officially, Intel's own D-Series card, formerly known as "Crescent Island", ships with 160 GB of LPDDR5X, and the company allows partners to go as high as 480 GB. The 512 GB figure is a bit odd when you look at the hardware. The leaked "Crescent Island" PCB from May showed 20 LPDDR5X sites, 12 on the front and eight on the back, each with an 8 GB package for 160 GB in total. Moving to 24 GB packages gets you neatly to 480 GB, while 512 GB doesn't divide evenly across 20 sites.
The D-Series itself is an inference-focused accelerator built on Xe3P with 32 cores, 1.5 TB/s of memory bandwidth and up to 1.3 PFLOPS of FP8 compute. It's a 350 W, air-cooled PCIe 5.0 x16 card with no display or 3D graphics hardware, so gamers shouldn't get their hopes up, and earlier leaks already suggested Xe3P would skip Arc gaming cards altogether. Customer sampling is underway, but pricing and availability are still unknown. A 512 GB partner card, if it exists, would likely cost a small fortune. Braw, investigadora sénior del Atlantic Council, un centro de estudios con sede en Washington, dirige la iniciativa sobre amenazas al orden marítimo global de esa institución. Cada año se dañan entre 150 y 200 cables en todo el mundo, y en general se reparan con rapidez.

- AI is getting cheaper and more capable, but the underlying hardware is not
- Infrastructure providers for the AI boom could be left holding the bag
Since the release of ChatGPT in late 2022, AI developers have entered into a frenzied arms race of hyperscaler data center build outs, silicon development, and huge power grid expansions.
The level of investment made by AI developers is unlike anything that has been seen (or spent) before. But a key question that IT leaders, investors, and enthusiasts keep asking is how will all this investment be paid for?
New analysis by Marin Ivezic, Founder of Applied Quantum, has found that the math really isn’t adding up. In order to justify the colossal investment, AI would need to generate approximately $2.5 trillion in annual revenue. Current estimates aren’t even close.
AI must replace 250 million jobs
Optimistic estimates put AI’s current revenues at between $150 billion and $250 billion per year, which is a multi-trillion shortfall.
Ivezic theorizes that AI would need to replace or deliver the equivalent productivity gains of 250 million full-time jobs in order to meet the $2.5 trillion revenue requirement - assuming each full-time employee costs $100,000.

articles.title: Elon Musk balance un indice capital sur le prochain vol de Starship : une première historique pourrait avoir lieu

Le 28 septembre dernier, Starship atteignait l’orbite pour la toute première fois lors de son 14e vol d’essai. Une étape majeure lors de laquelle 26 satellites Starlink V3 ont été déployés. Mais désormais, les yeux sont rivés vers le 15e test. Ce samedi 10 octobre, Elon Musk l’a justement évoqué lors d’une prise de parole lors de l’événement X Takeover. Et nous allons visiblement avoir droit à du spectacle.

Why better observability starts with better telemetry
For technology teams, connecting telemetry has traditionally been seen as a route to greater visibility. The assumption is straightforward: the more information available about what is happening across an environment, the easier it should be to understand problems and respond to them.
But as modern technology environments have grown in scale and complexity, that equation no longer looks quite so simple and teams have found themselves dealing with fragmented telemetry and unclear signals. It now takes longer to understand what’s gone wrong, and even longer to fix it. And to add to the challenge further, the cost of storing and processing all this telemetry and data continues to be on the rise.
Vice President of Sales for Log Management at Dynatrace.
This is prompting organizations to reconsider where the problem should be addressed. Rather than collecting everything and attempting to make sense of it later, attention is shifting towards improving telemetry earlier in its lifecycle. Filtering, enriching and directing it from the outset can make the information reaching teams more relevant and ultimately easier to act on.

articles.title: Cisco Warns of Active Attacks Exploiting New Critical Secure Email Gateway Vulnerability
articles.summary:
Attackers are exploiting a critical flaw in Cisco Secure Email Gateway that lets a sender with no login write files to the appliance's operating system, Cisco said in an advisory on Wednesday.
The attacker sends an email with a crafted attachment through the gateway and, if it succeeds, could then run commands as root. The appliance filters an organization's email for spam, malware, and other threats, and only a gateway with the File Reputation service enabled and a Content Scanner Tools package older than version 25.3.0.5525 is vulnerable.
The fix has been shipping since September 14 in AsyncOS 15.5.5-014 and 16.5.0-780, the builds Cisco listed as fixed in a hardening release that day, which the company now says covered this flaw. It also arrives as a Content Scanner Tools update, version 25.3.0.5525 or later, which installs without a software upgrade or a restart.
Cisco found the flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-76519 (CVSS score: 9.8), in its own internal security scanning and became aware of the attacks in October. The advisory does not say how many devices were attacked, who is behind the attacks, or whether the attackers obtained root on any of them.
Cisco has contacted customers of its managed Secure Email Cloud service whose devices showed "indicators of possible compromise" and says it is engaged in remediation and recovery. Threat actors are exploiting a critical security flaw in Langflow, according to an alert from Previdian.
Langflow is an open-source platform that allows developers to build artificial intelligence (AI) applications and agentic workflows. In February 2025, DataStax, the parent company of Langflow, was acquired by IBM.
The vulnerability in question is CVE-2026-105740 (CVSS score: 9.9), a case of authenticated remote code execution impacting versions prior to 1.9.0.
"Any authenticated Langflow user can achieve Remote Code Execution (RCE) on the server by adding an MCP server with the 'stdio' transport," reads an advisory released last month.
"The user-supplied command field is passed directly to bash -c "exec {command}" with zero validation, no allowlisting, and no sandboxing. The command executes immediately when the server list is fetched. Additionally, the env field allows arbitrary environment variable injection (e.g., LD_PRELOAD, PATH override)."
The crux of the vulnerability is that Langflow accepts a user-provided command without restricting it to approved executables. This, in turn, can lead to shell execution.

- Login as a regular, non-admin user.
- Add a malicious MCP server by sending a crafted HTTP POST request to "/api/v2/mcp/servers/{server_name}" with a command field containing a malicious payload (e.g., a reverse shell).

The credential-theft campaign known as GhostAction has ramped up, targeting more than 30,000 repositories across 3,000 users and organizations.
The spike, according to GitGuardian, was observed on October 8 and 9, 2026.
"This resulted from compromising the GitHub accounts of about 1,900 users. It attempted to extract 3,174 secrets from public repositories' CI," security researchers Gaetan Ferry and Guillaume Valadon said.
GhostAction is the moniker for a supply chain attack campaign targeting developer infrastructure on GitHub. Originally discovered in September 2025, it involves threat actors compromising legitimate developer accounts to inject malicious GitHub Actions automation workflows into software repositories.
Attackers have been found to gain write access to repositories using stolen Personal Access Tokens (PATs) or credentials harvested from infostealer logs and dumps. Using the hijacked maintainer account, they push a malicious workflow file disguised under deceptive names such as Security Audit ("security-audit.yml") or GitHub Actions Security ("github_actions_security.yml").
The end goal of the activity is the large-scale theft of continuous integration and continuous deployment (CI/CD) secrets, cloud credentials, package registry tokens (like npm, PyPI, and DockerHub), and artificial intelligence (AI) provider API keys.
A new wave of GhostAction has been observed since August 31, 2026, with the malicious workflow pushed to hundreds of repositories.

articles.title: Why AI Confidence Is Not Validation
articles.summary:
AI is already part of digital forensics and incident response work, with or without a policy in place to govern it. The issue is that these tools are growing more confident in their own output faster than practitioners are developing reliable ways to verify it. Without governance models and validation standards in place, that gap compounds and rarely stays contained to a workstation: an unverified finding can end up in a forensic report, a deposition, or in court.
At SANS, we created two new AI frameworks this year to help address this challenge: the Digital Forensics & AI Investigations Framework, which we mapped to the trusted standards established by the Scientific Working Group on Digital Evidence (SWGDE), and the Incident Response & AI Investigations Framework, which we mapped to the NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0. Both frameworks rest on the same principle: AI can accelerate investigative work, but the human examiner remains the final authority at every phase.
Where Validation Cannot Be Delegated
In digital forensics, validating an AI finding starts at the source file. A tool that doesn't show its reasoning has already produced an unreliable result, regardless of the confidence score attached to it. A tool that cites the specific file it parsed — for example, a claim that browser history came from Chrome's own database — gives an examiner somewhere to start. The claim is plausible at face value, but it still has to be confirmed independently before anyone treats it as…
