articles.title: Cómo resumir cualquier documento largo con solo usar mi voz y una frase secreta
articles.summary:
El prompt para resumir PDFs muy extensos con Gemini o ChatGPT debe definir la tarea, el formato de la respuesta y las restricciones de la herramienta. Pedir solo “resumí esto” puede producir una síntesis superficial, con conceptos omitidos o con menor atención sobre los contenidos que aparecen en las páginas centrales.
La frase ideal no busca únicamente acortar un archivo. Debe pedir que la IA identifique la tesis del documento, ordene argumentos, recupere fechas, cifras y nombres, y mantenga separados los datos comprobables de cualquier información que no figure en el PDF.
Un buen prompt para un PDF de más de 50 o 100 páginas debe solicitar primero un mapa de temas y luego un resumen por secciones cuando el archivo sea muy denso. Además, tiene que prohibir expresamente que la IA invente, complete vacíos o incorpore datos tomados de otras fuentes.
Antes de cargar el archivo, conviene comprobar si el PDF contiene texto seleccionable. Si se trata de páginas escaneadas como imágenes, debe pasar primero por un servicio de reconocimiento óptico de caracteres, conocido como OCR. Sin esa conversión, la herramienta puede no leer todo el documento.
Por qué no conviene pedir un resumen general a Gemini y ChatGPT
Los documentos extensos plantean un problema frecuente: la inteligencia artificial puede retener la introducción y las conclusiones, pero simplificar demasiado los capítulos centrales. Una petición general tampoco obliga a recuperar números, nombres, fechas o instrucciones, y u…

Drupal core has a critical flaw in its Field UI module that could let an attacker run code on the site's server, and fixes were shipped on October 14 in Drupal 11.4.10, 11.3.19, and 10.6.19.
An attacker cannot reach the flaw through core alone, the Drupal Security Team said in its advisory. Several exploit paths exist through contributed modules, and at least one known path needs no login.
Tracked as CVE-2026-108097, the flaw sits in Field UI, the core module behind the admin pages where site builders manage fields and how they display. Drupal rates it 19 out of 25 on its own risk scale, the level the project calls critical.
The advisory does not name the contributed modules that open a path to the flaw, and custom code may also expose it. Drew Webber of the Security Team and Octavio Galland are credited with reporting it.
What to Do Now
The fixed release for each supported branch:
- Drupal 11.4.x: update to 11.4.10
- Drupal 11.3.x: update to 11.3.19
- Drupal 10.6.x: update to 10.6.19
- Drupal 12.0.0 beta: 12.0.0-beta2, which is not for production use
- No fix: Drupal 11.2.x and below, 10.5.x and below, and Drupal 8 and 9, all of which are end-of-life
Both 11.3.x and 10.6.x lose security coverage in December 2026.
In the week starting October 4, 151,442 of the 531,499 sites that reported their Drupal core version to drupal.org (28.5%) were on a branch that the advisory lists as affected and that received no fix.

articles.title: NGINX Fixes 5 Flaws, Including Possible RCE and a TLS Bug That May Skip Client-Cert Checks
articles.summary:
NGINX released versions 1.30.6 and 1.31.7 on October 14 to fix five vulnerabilities, one of them present in every release since May 2005.
There are three memory bugs that F5, the company behind NGINX, says could crash a worker process or possibly let an attacker run code, and each requires a specific configuration to exploit.
A fourth lets an attacker forge a TLS session that could get past client-certificate checks, though F5 calls the forgery non-deterministic and beyond the attacker's control. The fifth lets an HTTP/3 client slip extra bytes into a request that NGINX passes on to a backend.
None of the five was in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog as of October 15, and neither NGINX nor F5 reports attacks. NGINX rates all five medium. F5 scores the three memory bugs 9.2, Critical, on CVSS v4.0, the TLS flaw 8.3, and the HTTP/3 flaw 6.9.
Which Configurations Are Exposed
Every one of the five needs a directive you added: an alias with a rewrite, a regex map, AIO with SSI, a shared TLS session cache, or HTTP/3. NGINX's own documentation recommends the shared session cache and request buffering; the other condition for the HTTP/3 flaw is on by default.
The TLS flaw sits in the automatic rotation of session ticket keys. Session tickets let a client resume a TLS session without a full handshake, and since version 1.23.2, from October 2022, a shared session cache makes NGINX generate and rotate the ticket keys itself unless you load keys from a file.

Candiru, an Israeli maker of spyware sold to governments, infected devices at the news network Al Jazeera through ordinary online ads, in attacks that needed no click or other action from the user, researchers at the Citizen Lab said Thursday.
The hidden attack code ran the moment an ad loaded on the screen, and in some cases the ad loaded out of sight, in the background.
The Citizen Lab, a research group at the University of Toronto, said this is the first public, technical confirmation that mercenary spyware, meaning hacking tools sold to governments, has reached real devices through targeted ads. The method had been described before from leaked company documents, but not shown in a live attack.
The researchers recovered the spyware itself from one device, but not the exploit that breaks into the browser or app to install it. That first break-in step is described from how the attack was set up, not from captured code.

The ads were placed by Discover-Tech, an Israeli company that presents itself as a normal digital advertising firm. Each ad carried a small piece of code that, when the ad loaded, quietly sent the device's advertising ID and internet address back to a Discover-Tech server, the researchers found.

Bank of America had to hire 1,000 contractors to patch software flaws spotted by Anthropic Mythos
It also had to spent more than a hundred million dollars
- Bank of America hired 1,000 contractors and spent hundreds of millions fixing AI-discovered vulnerabilities
- Anthropic’s Mythos uncovered enough flaws to trigger large-scale remediation across major banks
- Financial institutions warn advanced AI security tools are exposing weaknesses faster than teams can patch them
Bank of America, one of the largest financial institutions in the United States, was forced to hire a thousand people on contractor roles, and spend north of a $100 million dollars to fix all of the bugs found by the famed Mythos, Anthropic’s generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) model.
When Anthropic first unveiled Mythos in April 2026, it described it as a tool with advanced cybersecurity capabilities that can autonomously discover and exploit previously unknown software vulnerabilities.
However, the tool was so capable (and dangerous) that Anthropic locked it down, giving access to a handful of vetted organizations: the US government, critical infrastructure organizations, banks, and some cybersecurity firms, to name a few.
Bank of America and JPMorgan Chase

articles.title: ‘The explosion of AI-generated content continues to impact the whole music ecosystem’: Deezer will let you ban AI music from your feed as YouTube Music adds warning labels for slop
articles.summary:
YouTube Music adds AI labels to warn you about slop — as Deezer goes further with new ‘on-off toggle’ for millions of AI-generated songs
Purify your feed
- YouTube Music says it will start labeling AI-generated music tracks
- On Deezer, you’ll be able to exclude AI music from your feed entirely
- Both platforms say there is a clear user demand for transparency
AI-generated music is a controversial topic in the world of streaming platforms, with the likes of Apple Music saying that over a third of its uploads are “100% AI.” Now, both YouTube Music and Deezer are taking steps to make it easier to spot artificially created tunes — and purge them from your listening feeds altogether.
The Google-owned YouTube Music has just announced that both the YouTube Music and YouTube apps will actively flag tracks that have been “created primarily using generative AI,” the company said in a press release. These labels will be attached to the app’s player page and will include a pop-up window with more information on how AI might have been used.
Music streaming service Deezer has gone a step further and has told users it will introduce a new toggle before the end of 2026 that will let them “avoid AI-generated music completely.” Deezer says that this will “improve the user experience” and put “full focus on discovering human creators.”

articles.title: Airbnb’s latest update brings AI search, easier property comparisons, and more services

Airbnb adds AI search and more services to help you plan your next getaway
More natural search to help you find a property
- Airbnb is adding AI-powered search
- New AI comparisons make it easier to weigh up vacation rentals and narrow down your options
- Services are expanding to include baby-gear rentals, laundry, and meal delivery.
After a major redesign of its entire service, headed by an easier-to-use app for iOS and Android, Airbnb is further refining the experience to make finding your next vacation rental a little easier. Not surprisingly, it’s turning to AI, but the focus here is on natural-language search, property comparisons, and updated ways to find what else you can do while staying at your Airbnb.
This follow-up should make it easier to find homes, experiences, or services that meet your needs — the three main parts of the redesigned app. Instead of introducing a new interface or updated visuals, Airbnb is using AI to help you find what you’re looking for more easily. Pushing aside sorting through filters, lists, and checkboxes, you’ll be able to search for a stay the way you’d actually talk about it.
The quest to make searching easier
Like Claude or ChatGPT, Airbnb’s new AI search lets you type or speak a query, making it easier to find a stay that fits what you have in mind. You can search across homes, experiences, and services, using your own words to describe what you need, rather than trying to find the right combination of filters.

articles.title: Missing Microsoft Publisher? LibreOffice is here to save the day
articles.summary:
Missing Microsoft Publisher? LibreOffice is here to save the day
LibreOffice now supports Publisher files
- Microsoft has officially retired Publisher and ended support
- .pub is a proprietary file format, but the app used to access it has gone
- LibreOffice reverse-engineered the format so that you can use the Draw app
Microsoft has quietly ended more than three decades of Publisher after pulling support for Microsoft 365 subscribers earlier in October 2026 – even perpetual license under Publisher 2021 lost support following the company's decision.
While .pub files aren't set to be deleted, Microsoft fans will no longer be able to view and edit them, and are instead being told to move over to Word, PowerPoint or another suitable app.
But LibreOffice just declared its support, throwing Publisher users a lifeline – and it was a lot harder than you might've thought.
LibreOffice had to reverse-engineer Publisher
"From today, these documents are in a proprietary format, the only fully compatible application for which has been abandoned by the very company that created it," Italo Vignoli wrote, noting that the developers behind the Document Liberation Project had to reverse-engineer the .pub format, which isn't an open standard.
As a result, Publisher fans can now finally open .pub files with LibreOffice Draw, but that's only part of the news because LibreOffice's Italo Vignoli went on to slate Microsoft for forcing users into a vendor lock-in, restricting their access to controls…
